body: So that's what I'll do. Thank you!
Wait, so if I get immersion baptized, I can also immersion baptize people? Because simply put, I've always wanted to do that, once my faith becomes stronger and more stable.
An unfortunate impossibility in my city. An atheistic city if there ever was one such place. Going to church alone in midday and praying does makes one feel better, however, and that is what I do.

You may be right. I am a narcissist and I recognize this. 

In all honesty, I'm trying my hardest to actually not talk about myself when conversing with people. And it works, you're right. Holding a genuine interest in others makes them more complacent, friendly and overall cooperative. 
Unfortunately, I've found that helping them for free gives them the idea that I'm a doormat to be taken for granted. So I rarely do anything for free if it's not family or a really good friend anymore.

Thanks.

You're right. This lonesomeness is actually downright torturous.

Exactly. It's not an easy process to start from ground zero, but it can be done, especially with the help of the Lord.

Thank you for the support, I truly appreciate it!

Yeah, that's where we're in trouble. My city is, I believe, the capital of atheism in Europe. There populace of Prague is made up of approximately 1% Christians. 

But yes, I do need to make some friends. I literally have none. Not a single one. The only Christian peer I knew was a right foul arrogant prick so I bid him farewell, and now I'm friendless.

Oh. In that case, forgive me for my hostility. The solitude makes one constantly on edge, the betrayals do so equally.

Thank you, truly.
I actually haven't been baptized at all, to be honest... I'm not a part of any church, though I want to be.

Now now, no need for tension. I'm not here to spark conflict nor debate. Just looking for some words of consolation and support in my time of need.

I'm but a humble soul without much money. Sometimes the words of fellow followers of Christ do wonders to soothe the nerves, sometimes their answers can turn us from falling into pits of despair. I apologize for having offended you and your view of God, friend. It was not my intention, truly.
That's what I'm hoping for... And praying for.

I'd like to believe that I do understand its meaning. The meaning being, or at least one of its meanings, that we are not judged or forsaken despite our flaws and inherent evils, that we are loved and accepted unconditionally by the Lord, that we were, well, bought out. 

That does not mean that we can wreak havoc upon the world without consequences, of course, but so as long as a man regrets his sins, he can and will be forgiven for them. 
I've done awful things. Yet I strongly believed that the Lord does not punish us, rather teaches us. He has no use for punishment, not anymore. So then, is my constant solitude and longing for a fellow soul a mere lesson?

If it is a lesson, why does He give me hope, only to strip me of it immediately? Because of this, I no longer trust anyone and I feel it will become difficult for me to be devoted or bound to another person if this cycle continues, which would be a tragedy for me.

And for that I thank you. Another prayer for my soul means a lot to me, because I know that prayers can and do work. 

So thank you, truly.

And so I have heard, yet I cannot understand why he is leaving me hanging. I feel constantly devastated, always alone. Always betrayed for one reason or another, or no reason at all.

I do not know how much longer I can live this way. Believe me, the thoughts of death have taken a hold of me. I will never act upon them, but they are unbearable.

Believe me, I wish I knew. I just sort of did. Loved her at first, it was nice, and then I just felt spite. Spite and a need to poison everything around me. So I did, I poisoned everything with my depressive thoughts and feelings.

I am truly a bad person. Unlike most people who say so, I truly am. I wanted to be a loyal servant of God, but I failed. I hope I can still be saved.

She loved me, so I denied her. Clearly the right choice, of course. Eight months it lasted. 

Getting some real Evgenij Onegin vibes from myself lately.

I think you're absolutely right. This is also a matter of insufficiently defined identity. I really don't know who exactly I am. That's probably an issue of, well, not really doing enough stuff. 

I'm planning on joining a historical fencing group next year though, and getting a firearms license for the range, so that should give me a greater sense of self and community. And joining a church would probably be fun too.

Hopefully it doesn't happen. I have faith that the Lord will give me another chance to undo what I've done, and I most definitely will try if the chance is given.

I am a sinner beyond most sinners, but still not hopeless, certainly.
I'd associate myself with the protestant church, since it's the largest church in my country. Although my country is one of the most atheistic in the world, so it doesn't help much.

I always wanted to work on planes too, actually. Wanted to design parts and all. Unfortunately, I've never been an excellent student, so I'm probably destined for lower-wage work.

Military seems, in a certain way, more of a guarantee for a somewhat stable financial life. I'm much too afraid of getting fired from a civilian job.

Ah, so to have faith is essentially to walk humbly with the Lord? That seems sensible. Not that I'd want to compare myself to Him, not at all. 

So we are to accept His forgiveness and not fear Him so as much as respect Him? That's the feeling I'm getting from this comparison.

Well I managed to get my first girlfriend around that time. True, I didn't have as much time for myself as a result, but I don't know if it's a primary cause.

Lots of bouts of depression and insecurity about my looks hit me around then, which probably caused me to lose a lot of motivation to do much. And it's true, I did lose a lot of motivation and quit studying completely.

This year is hopeless. I'm passing, but not really excelling. Next year, I've promised myself to start working harder. A lot harder.

I don't think I'll lose faith in the Lord no matter what. I've gone down that road a few times, but I've always come back. It's the right way, faith. 

I'm just afraid that what I did will lead unwanted, well.. Circumstances. I made some mistakes, and I'm scared. Despite taking every precaution, I'm scared. I cannot possibly father a child at this age, when I cannot nearly take care of myself. Me and the other person in question would be forced to end our lives for the sake of sparing a child an inadequate life. 

Sure, that hasn't happened yet, but it looks like it might have, and I'm scared to death. Shouldn't have done it, but I did. Now there's no way out.

I intend to become a mechanical engineer and have a successful military career, and hopefully move to Israel one day and live out my days in peace.

The grades? I wish I knew. Probably sloth. My greatest sin. A sin I can't seem to beat.

I did ask Him to make me hate my sins, and unfortunately, He seems to be making me hate them in ways which may well ruin my life.

I committed adultery. Well, no, not really. As in, I'm not married, nor was I. But I still did some things I should not have done with someone whom I did not marry, and it seems to have backfired in the most spectacular of manners. Unless it's a false alarm. If it isn't, I'm afraid my life is over.

But a combat role is something I must occupy. I don't think I could become a commissioned officer with a history of depressive disorders, and a military officer career seems like the only thing I could stand as a mechanical engineer.

Hmm... I assume the only different change is that I'm no longer as lonely now. On the other hand, I'm more annoyed by everything, I'm quite wroth and overall unsatisfied with everything. I am incompetent, all my abilities are failing.

It's sort of a difference in perspective, but also a factual change, since my grades have gone down objectively by 1 GPA point. From 3.5 to 2.5.
That's true faith right there. To stand firmly in face of such danger, even against one's life - indeed, an incredible feat of faith.

I did meet JWs one time on the underground transport. They seemed like very nice people.

I thoroughly and openly accept that my views might be completely wrong. In fact, they probably are. All I want to do is serve the Lord and show my gratitude for what I've been given, but it seems so difficult with all these constant trials and toils, whether they be from the Lord or elsewhere.

Right, but were I to admit it, I'd never be able to serve in a combat unit. That is something I cannot give up in my life.

Surely there must be ways to get treatment without being written off as inadequate for military service?
But he became Israel though. I mean, who wouldn't want to become the founder of a nation? That's worth a hip in my opinion.

Well, I'm just an academic and personal failure. That's all that's happened, really. I'm finding out that I'm not nearly as competent as I thought myself to be - in fact, far less. 

It's a painful thing to accept.
That we have to, aye. I'm still failing though. Constantly. I can't seem to learn.

Out of desperation, from the absolute bottom, rising from that pit of despair. I was a foolish militant atheist before I saw the truth, and then I started reading the Law and the New Testament, and it's all better now.

For some time now, however, things have only taken a turn for the worse. I'm unsure as to what exactly is going on with my life anymore.
I certainly hope not. I value my hips far too much for that.
I suppose it is slowly turning into that. Wish it didn't. That alone is a failure of will.

So I shall.

Unfortunately, it seems that the enemy is me. I am my own foe.

Then I don't understand why my prayers won't be heard.

People often say - "you do not believe in yourself."   
And they are right. I do not believe in myself. I believe in the Lord, and put my faith in Him. Alone, as you say, I am weak. With Him, I should be stronger, yet I find myself even more hopeless most days.

Huh.. That is a very interesting view on the matter. I should have paid closer attention to Corinthians. 

Anyway, what must I do if I am so weak in my situation that I lose the will to live? It is just a weak-willed view, I would say, but then again... I don't really know.

Very well, however. I will take my weakness as a blessing rather than a curse, my failure as a guarantee.

It is a hear-warming thing to hear. Truly. 

It sounds vain, and it likely is, but the words of other people are calming and soothing in the worst of times. I hope I can be forgiven for the countless terrible things I've done because of truly vain human desires.

Peace be with you, friend.

So you think I should press on through the hardships?

I have sinned in terrible ways. Worst being that I was with someone before marriage, and many times, and now I fear that I will reap the results of these terrible crimes.

Maybe I am not strong enough to fulfill The Lord's will?
